What Are Benzos?

blocks.html: Benzos are a class of medications called benzodiazepines. These medications are controlled substances that are often prescribed for people who struggle with anxiety and insomnia disorders. Benzos are available in long-acting, intermediate-acting, and short-acting pills.

Are Benzos Addictive?

blocks.html: Benzos are controlled substances, meaning there is a risk of developing an addiction to them. Like other controlled substances, benzos cause a surge of dopamine in our brains, impacting our natural reward system. This surge is enjoyable and often leads to the individual repeating the behavior so they can experience a similar effect.

Like other controlled substances, benzos cause a surge of dopamine in our brains, impacting our natural reward system. blocks.html: Regular use of benzos, even if taken as prescribed, can increase a person’s risk for physical dependence. This is characterized by developing tolerance and experiencing withdrawal symptoms when reducing or stopping the medication.

Do Benzos Cause Withdrawal?

blocks.html: A common component of physical dependence and addiction to benzos is the presence of withdrawal symptoms. Withdrawal can occur when someone tries to reduce their dose or stops using it. This can be an uncomfortable, painful, and life-threatening experience. It is important to note that serious health concerns can arise during the benzo detox, so it is strongly recommended that you speak with a doctor before you make any changes to your typical benzo intake. What Are Common Benzo Withdrawal Symptoms?

blocks.html:
There are a variety of symptoms associated with benzo withdrawal. Again, it is important to note that some of the symptoms associated with benzo withdrawal can be life treating and warrant immediate medical attention.

Physical signs associated with withdrawal include:
- Nausea
- Sweating
- Headaches
- Heart palpitations
- Muscle pain
- Tremors
- Anxiety
- Panic attacks
- Seizures

The length of time that you experience withdrawal symptoms will depend on the specific medication you have been taking, as they vary in different half-lives. How to Detox from Benzos
Get the Help You Need

blocks.html: The first step in detoxing from benzos is seeking medical support. If you have been misusing or abusing a prescription, you can speak to your provider. If you have been taking benzos without a prescription, your primary care physician can support you.
blocks.text: The first step in detoxing from benzos is seeking medical support. If you have been misusing or abusing a prescription, you can speak to your provider. If you have been taking benzos without a prescription, your primary care physician can support you.

blocks.html: When you meet with a medical professional, they will talk to you about your different detoxing options. The method of detoxing that is appropriate for you will be dependent on a few factors, including the specific medication you have been abusing, the dosage you take, any underlying mental health concerns, how you abuse the medication, and the use of any other substances.

blocks.html: Depending on the severity of your use, your doctor can recommend that you detox on an outpatient basis or within an inpatient treatment program. The benefit of being in an inpatient treatment facility is that you will have around-the-clock medical supervision. Outpatient detoxing is reserved for individuals who have a low risk of experiencing dangerous side effects.
